The Helicopter Company (THC) is a Saudi commercial helicopter operator owned by the Public Investment Fund, launched in 2020. It flies passenger and tourism charters, medical evacuation, offshore oil and gas support, VIP transport and urban air mobility pilots, using a growing fleet of Airbus, Leonardo and other helicopters. Customers are government bodies, energy companies, hospitals, giga-projects such as NEOM and Red Sea, and tourists. Based in Riyadh; Crunchbase shows a SAR 600 million funding event in July 2025. Strong national profile in Saudi Arabia but little consumer brand awareness elsewhere.

Trackforce Valiant provides software for the private security guarding industry, with mobile apps and a workforce platform for scheduling, guard tours, incident reporting and payroll. It was formed through the combination of Trackforce and Valiant, backed by private equity, with $150 million raised in September 2019. Customers are security guard companies and facilities that employ patrol officers, mainly in North America. It earns subscription software fees. Based in Southlake, Texas. B2B enterprise software with little consumer visibility, so limited sponsorship appeal beyond corporate hospitality.

Yuanbao is a Chinese internet insurance platform, set up by Beijing-based Yuanbao Insurance Research, that sells health and other insurance products online to consumers and earns commissions from insurers. Crunchbase shows total funding of about $157 million, with the latest round in April 2025. It is headquartered in Beijing's Chaoyang district. Customers are individual Chinese policyholders reached through mobile channels and partner platforms. Domestic consumer fintech brand with moderate awareness in China and almost none abroad.

Yunfeng Financial Group is a Hong Kong-listed financial services holding company based in Wan Chai, associated with Yunfeng Capital, the private equity firm co-founded by Jack Ma and David Yu. Its activities have centred on insurance and wealth-related businesses, including a stake in MassMutual Asia, alongside asset management and fintech services for Chinese and Hong Kong clients, earning fees, commissions and investment income. Crunchbase shows HK$1.17 billion in funding, latest in September 2025. Low consumer brand recognition outside Greater China.

Nerdy is a US online learning company behind the Varsity Tutors brand, offering live one-to-one and group tutoring, test preparation and AI-assisted learning tools. It sells to families directly and to schools and districts, plus an enterprise segment, earning session and subscription revenue. Headquartered in St. Louis, Missouri, and founded as Varsity Tutors in 2007. It went public via a SPAC merger in 2021 and trades on the NYSE under NRDY, with annual revenue near $190 million. Recognizable US education consumer brand with national advertising, but modest global profile.

PLAY was an Icelandic low-cost airline based in Reykjavik, operating from Keflavik airport since 2021. It flew Airbus A320 and A321neo family aircraft on routes between Iceland, Europe and North America, selling point-to-point and connecting transatlantic tickets to leisure travellers, with ancillary fees. It was listed on Nasdaq First North Iceland under the ticker PLAY, and the Crunchbase figure shows about $145 million raised. The airline ceased operations in late September 2025 after failing to stabilise its finances. Known mostly to Icelandic and transatlantic budget travellers; no longer an active prospect.

Seanergy Maritime Holdings is a Greek shipping company based in Glyfada, Athens, owning a fleet of Capesize dry bulk vessels that carry iron ore, coal and grain for charterers under time charters and spot voyages. It is listed on Nasdaq under the ticker SHIP and is incorporated in the Marshall Islands. Crunchbase shows about $146 million in funding, latest in July 2026. Its customers are commodity traders and mining and steel groups. B2B shipping with essentially no consumer brand visibility.

Valamar Riviera is Croatia's largest tourism company, headquartered in Porec in Istria. It owns and runs hotels, resorts and campsites under the Valamar, Sunny and Camping Adriatic brands, mainly along the Istrian and Dalmatian coasts and Dubrovnik, with roughly 30 properties plus Austrian-market accommodation. Customers are leisure holidaymakers, largely from Germany, Austria, Slovenia and Italy, and revenue comes from room, food and beverage sales. It is listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange (ZSE: RIVP). Well known regional hospitality brand but not a global consumer name.

Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Bogota, known as ETB, is a Colombian telecommunications operator headquartered in Bogota. It sells fixed broadband, fibre internet, television, landline telephony and mobile services to households, businesses and government clients, mainly in the capital region. The Bogota district government is its majority shareholder, so it is largely state-owned, and its shares are listed on the Colombian stock exchange. Crunchbase shows about $102 million in funding, latest in September 2026. Regional consumer brand with strong local recognition in Bogota and little abroad.

Hanjin KAL is the holding company of the Hanjin Group in South Korea, based in Seoul and the parent of Korean Air through its stake in Korean Air Lines, plus Hotel Hanjin, Jin Air stakes and Hanjin Transportation interests. Its income comes from dividends and brand royalties from the group's airline, hotel, logistics and aerospace businesses. It is listed on the Korea Exchange. Crunchbase shows large funding of about 126 billion won, latest in July 2026. The group is owned by the Cho family. Holding company with limited direct consumer exposure, though Korean Air has strong brand visibility.

Hexatronic Group is a Swedish fibre optic infrastructure company based in Gothenburg. It makes and sells fibre cables, ducts, connectivity and installation systems for telecom operators, data centres and utilities, with operations in Sweden, Germany, the US, the UK and Asia, and acquisitions such as Raycap's fibre business. Revenue is in the billions of Swedish kronor. Customers are network builders and telecoms. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under HTRO, and the Crunchbase figure shows SEK 1.1 billion raised, latest in May 2026. B2B supplier with little public brand awareness.

Loctek Ergonomic Technology is a Chinese manufacturer based in Ningbo, Zhejiang, making height-adjustable standing desks, monitor arms and ergonomic office furniture, plus lifting systems for healthcare beds. It works as an OEM and also sells under its own brands, including Flexispot, via e-commerce in North America and Europe. Customers are retailers, online shoppers and healthcare equipment makers. It is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. Crunchbase shows about CN 700 million in funding, last in September 2021. Flexispot has solid online consumer recognition in the West.

NAVYA was a French maker of autonomous electric shuttles and driverless vehicles, based in Villeurbanne near Lyon and founded in 2014. Its Autonom Shuttle and Autonom Cab were used on campuses, airports and city pilots for public transport operators and industrial sites. It was listed on Euronext Growth Paris but ran into financial trouble and entered receivership in 2023, after which it was taken over by Gaussin Macnica Mobility. Crunchbase shows about 101 million in funding, latest in October 2022. Niche B2B brand, well covered in mobility press.

Nordic Semiconductor is a Norwegian fabless semiconductor company based in Trondheim, a leading maker of low-power wireless chips for Bluetooth Low Energy, Thread, Zigbee, Wi-Fi, cellular IoT and Matter. Its nRF series chips are inside wearables, hearing aids, smart home devices, medical equipment and consumer electronics, and it sells to device manufacturers worldwide, with design centres across Europe, the US and Asia. Revenue is around NOK 5 to 6 billion. Listed on Oslo Bors under NOD. B2B component supplier with strong engineering reputation but little consumer awareness.

Al Tawfeek for Financial Leasing is a finance company based in Giza, Egypt, active in the Finance and Financial Services sector and apparently in leasing. Crunchbase reports funding of EGP 3.299 billion, with the latest event dated December 2025, and the entry is flagged as coming from a search of listed companies, which suggests it is publicly traded in Egypt. No further detail on its products, customers, owners or scale is available from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Insta360 is a consumer imaging brand, 360-degree and action camera maker founded in 2015 by Arashi Vision in Shenzhen, China, with a major US presence in Los Angeles. Its products include the X series 360 cameras, Ace Pro action cameras, GO tiny cameras and Flow gimbals, sold online and through retailers in many countries to creators, travellers and sports enthusiasts. Revenue runs into the billions of yuan. Arashi Vision listed on the Shanghai STAR Market in 2025. Strong sports and creator brand awareness, directly competing with GoPro.

Matrimony.com is an Indian online matchmaking and wedding services company based in Chennai, founded in 2000 by Murugavel Janakiraman. It runs BharatMatrimony and more than a dozen community matrimony sites, EliteMatrimony for premium users, and Assisted Service with offline centres, plus a wedding services marketplace. Customers are Indian families and diaspora users who pay subscription fees for paid memberships. It is listed on the NSE and BSE under MATRIMONY, with revenue around INR 4.5 billion. Very high brand recognition among Indian consumers and a heavy advertiser.

Siniora Food Industries is a Jordanian processed meat and food manufacturer based in Amman, known for the Siniora brand of sausages, frankfurters, burgers, ham, deli meats and ready meals, sold in Jordan, the Gulf, Iraq, Palestine and other Middle East markets. Customers are retailers, restaurants and households, and the company earns revenue from branded food sales through its own distribution network. Crunchbase shows $80 million in funding, latest in March 2024, and flags it as listed. Strong consumer brand visibility across the Levant, with limited reach outside the region.

Clavister is a Swedish cybersecurity company based in Ornskoldsvik, founded in 1997, that builds network security software and firewalls under the cOS Core and cOS Stream names. It sells to telecom operators, managed security service providers, governments and enterprises, and since 2020s increasingly to defence and military vehicle makers through its onWire and Defence Grade products, with Swedish and European customers. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under CLAV. Crunchbase shows about $39 million in funding. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

NIS is the leading Serbian oil and gas company, headquartered in Novi Sad. It explores and produces oil and gas, runs the Pancevo refinery, and sells fuels through about 400 Gazprom Neft and NIS Petrol filling stations in Serbia and neighbouring Balkan states, along with lubricants and energy services. Gazprom Neft owns a majority stake, with the Serbian state holding about 30 percent, and it trades on the Belgrade Stock Exchange (NIS). US sanctions on Russian owners hit the company in 2025. Strong consumer visibility in Serbia through its fuel stations.

Robin Energy is a small shipping company based in Limassol, Cyprus, operating product tankers that carry refined petroleum products for charterers. It is listed on Nasdaq under the ticker RBNE and was spun out of the Greek-Cypriot shipping group around Petros Panagiotidis. Crunchbase shows about $42 million in funding, latest in July 2026. Customers are oil traders and energy groups, and the fleet is only a few vessels. B2B maritime business with no consumer brand profile, so sponsorship fit is weak.

SpectrumOne is a Stockholm-based information technology company, flagged in Crunchbase as listed. The input supports only a general IT description with about $37.6 million in funding, latest in July 2026. It is not possible to confirm its exact products, customers, owners or scale from the available data, though the name suggests technology consulting or software services in the Swedish market. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

SRAX, formerly Social Reality Inc., is a US digital marketing and financial technology company based in Westlake Village, California, known for its Sequire investor-relations software platform and BIGtoken consumer data marketplace. It sold to public companies seeking to understand shareholders and to advertisers buying audience data. It was listed on Nasdaq under SRAX, but faced delayed filings and was delisted in 2023, with financial difficulties thereafter. Crunchbase shows about $52 million in funding. Small B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

Steakholder Foods, formerly MeaTech 3D, is an Israeli food technology company based in Rehovot, developing cultivated meat and fish and 3D bioprinting technology, and selling plant-based premixes and printers. It supplies food producers and licenses technology rather than selling to consumers directly, with partners in Europe and Asia including Umami Bioworks. It is listed on Nasdaq under STKH. Crunchbase shows about $41 million in funding, latest in July 2026. Pre-commercial alternative protein firm with small revenue and modest public awareness.

Tokens.com is a Canadian digital asset company based in Toronto that invests in and operates Web3 businesses, including metaverse real estate, NFTs and its Metaverse Group subsidiary, as well as cryptocurrency staking activities. It earns income from staking, investments and digital asset sales, serving crypto investors rather than consumers directly. It is listed on the Canadian NEO Exchange and OTC markets under COIN. Crunchbase shows about $38 million in funding, latest in October 2021. Visible in crypto media but a small company with limited mainstream awareness.

Zetrix is a Malaysian blockchain and digital infrastructure company based in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, that builds the Zetrix public blockchain, digital identity and tokenisation solutions for government and enterprises. It is linked to MYEG Services, the e-government services provider, and has been publicised for the Zetrix AI chain and Zetrix wallet in Malaysia and Asia. Crunchbase shows about $40 million raised, latest February 2026, and flags the company as listed. Mostly B2B and government projects, moderate awareness in Malaysia.

Naga is a German fintech and social trading group based in Hamburg, offering the NAGA trading app and platform where retail customers trade CFDs, stocks and crypto and copy other traders' portfolios, plus a Visa card and wallet. It earns trading spreads, fees and card income, serving retail clients in Europe, Asia and elsewhere, and is regulated through licences in Cyprus and Seychelles. The parent, The NAGA Group AG, is listed in Frankfurt under N4G. Crunchbase shows about $38 million in funding. Online brand with moderate consumer awareness in Europe.

Argo Mining is a company in the Blockchain and Cryptocurrency sector based in London, England, flagged by Crunchbase as a listed company. The input shows about $30.7 million in total funding, with the latest event in February 2021. It cannot be confirmed from the input what exactly it does, who its customers are, or how large it is, and it should not be assumed to be the same as any similarly named crypto miner. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Icon Energy is a shipping company based in Athens, Greece, operating in freight service and shipping, and flagged by Crunchbase as a listed company. The input shows about $32.4 million in total funding, latest in May 2026. It most likely charters vessels to commodity or energy traders, but the fleet, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the input. B2B maritime business with no clear consumer brand profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

People Can Fly is a Polish video game developer and publisher based in Warsaw, founded in 2002. It created Bulletstorm, Painkiller and Gears of War: Judgment, and has worked on Outriders, Gears 5 and projects for Square Enix and Sony, with studios in Poland, the UK, the US, Canada and Ireland. It earns income from development contracts, publishing and its own game sales to gamers worldwide. It is listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange under PCF. Crunchbase shows PLN 155 million in funding. Known in the gaming community but not a household name.

Suominen is a Finnish manufacturer of nonwoven materials based in Espoo. It produces wipes substrates and other nonwovens for baby wipes, household and personal care wipes and medical products, with plants in Finland, Italy, Brazil and the US and sales to major hygiene and consumer products brands worldwide. Revenue is around EUR 400 to 450 million. It is listed on Nasdaq Helsinki under SUY1V. Crunchbase shows about 28 million in funding, latest in June 2026. B2B supplier with little public brand recognition.

XTAO is a company in the Artificial Intelligence sector with its address in Grand Cayman, Cayman Islands, flagged by Crunchbase as listed. The input shows about $30.1 million in funding, latest in November 2025, and little more. The business model, customers, ownership and operating locations cannot be confirmed from the input. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Genmab is a Danish biotechnology company headquartered in Copenhagen's Valby, founded in 1999, that develops antibody therapeutics for cancer and other diseases. Its products include Darzalex for multiple myeloma, marketed by Johnson & Johnson with Genmab receiving royalties, Kesimpta with Novartis, Tivdak and Epkinly with partners, and it acquired ProfoundBio in 2024 and Merus in 2025-2026. Customers are pharma partners and healthcare systems. Revenue is in the billions of dollars and it is listed on Nasdaq (GMAB) and Copenhagen. Low consumer brand awareness.

Alibaba Bendi Shenghuo Fuwu is the holding entity for Alibaba Group's Local Services unit, which includes Ele.me food delivery and Koubei, based in Beijing. Alibaba bought out Ele.me in 2018 for about $9.5 billion and merged it with Koubei into a local services platform, supporting on-demand delivery and restaurant services for millions of Chinese consumers. Crunchbase shows $4 billion in funding in November 2018. A subsidiary of Alibaba Group (NYSE: BABA; HKEX: 9988). Consumer app with very high awareness in China, little outside.

Canopy Growth is a Canadian cannabis company headquartered in Smiths Falls, Ontario, founded in 2014 as Tweed. It grows and sells recreational cannabis brands such as Tweed, Tokyo Smoke, 7ACRES and Doja, medical cannabis, vapes and Storz & Bickel vaporizers, plus BioSteel sports drinks and Martha Stewart CBD. Customers are adult consumers, medical patients and Canadian provincial retailers, with sales in Germany and elsewhere. Constellation Brands invested more than $5 billion. It is listed on Nasdaq (CGC) and the TSX (WEED), with persistent losses. Known in the cannabis industry, restricted advertising.

Ele.me is a Chinese on-demand food delivery and local lifestyle platform, founded in Shanghai in 2008 and acquired by Alibaba in 2018. Customers order meals and groceries from restaurants and stores through an app, with riders delivering in hundreds of Chinese cities, and Ele.me earns commissions, delivery fees and advertising from merchants. It rebranded as part of Alibaba's local services business and is now integrated with Taobao Instant Commerce (Taobao Shangou). Crunchbase shows about $3.3 billion in funding. Huge consumer awareness in China, competing with Meituan, but no international presence.

Eli Lilly is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, headquartered in Indianapolis and founded in 1876. It develops and sells prescription medicines including the GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, Verzenio, Taltz, Jardiance with Boehringer Ingelheim, Humalog insulin and others, to health systems, pharmacies and patients in over 100 countries. Revenue exceeded $45 billion in 2024 and market capitalisation passed $700 billion in 2025. Listed on the NYSE under LLY. Major global corporate brand, though consumer promotion is limited by regulation.

Grifols is a Spanish healthcare company based in Sant Cugat del Valles near Barcelona, founded in 1909. It is one of the world's largest producers of plasma-derived medicines, operating hundreds of plasma donation centres mostly in the US, and also makes diagnostics, transfusion medicine products and hospital pharmacy supplies. Customers are hospitals, blood banks, health authorities and clinical labs, with sales in over 100 countries and revenue above EUR 6 billion. Listed on the Spanish stock exchange (GRF) with ADRs on Nasdaq (GRFS). B2B healthcare brand with low public awareness.

Labcorp is a US clinical laboratory and drug development group based in Burlington, North Carolina. Labcorp Diagnostics runs a large network of patient service centres and labs for physicians, hospitals and employers, while Labcorp Drug Development provides central lab and clinical trial services to pharma. It operates across the US, Europe and other markets, with revenue around $13 billion and more than 70,000 employees. Listed on the NYSE under LH. Well known among US patients and healthcare professionals, but primarily a B2B and healthcare brand.

Mowi is the world's largest producer of farmed Atlantic salmon, headquartered in Bergen, Norway. It runs hatcheries, sea farms, feed production and processing plants across Norway, Scotland, Canada, Chile, Ireland, the Faroe Islands and Iceland, selling fresh and value-added salmon products to supermarkets, food service and distributors in about 70 markets. Revenue is around EUR 5 billion and it employs over 11,000 people. Listed on Oslo Bors (MOWI). Consumer-facing branded products in Europe such as Mowi retail packs, though the company is largely a B2B supplier.

Olam International is a Singapore-based agri-business and food ingredients group, founded in 1989, trading and processing cocoa, coffee, cashews, spices, dairy, edible nuts, cotton and grains. Since 2022 it has operated through Olam Food Ingredients (ofi) and Olam Agri, with Saudi Arabia's SALIC buying a majority of Olam Agri. Customers are food, beverage and consumer goods manufacturers in around 60 countries, with revenue above $40 billion. Temasek's Aranda is the largest shareholder and the shares are listed on the SGX. B2B supplier with limited consumer awareness.

Shanghai RAAS Blood Products is a Chinese plasma products company based in Shanghai, producing human albumin, immunoglobulins and coagulation factors from donated plasma collected at its plasma stations. Customers are Chinese hospitals and healthcare systems, and revenue comes from sales of plasma-derived therapies. Spanish group Grifols took a minority stake in the company around 2019, and Haier Group became its controlling shareholder in the 2020s. Listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. B2B healthcare, with low consumer brand awareness. Crunchbase shows CN 25 billion in funding as read.

Syngenta Group is a Swiss-headquartered agricultural technology group based in Basel, wholly owned by state-owned Sinochem Holdings of China since the 2017 acquisition of Syngenta AG for $43 billion. It sells crop protection chemicals, seeds, digital farming tools and, via Adama and Syngenta Group China, a wide agricultural portfolio to farmers and distributors in over 100 countries. Revenue is about $28 billion. An IPO on the Shanghai STAR Market was withdrawn in 2024. B2B agricultural brand, high recognition among farmers and limited among consumers.

Echo Global Logistics was a US third-party logistics provider based in Chicago that arranged truckload, less-than-truckload, intermodal and managed transportation services for shippers, using a technology platform and a large carrier network. It was listed on Nasdaq under ECHO from 2009 and was acquired by The Jordan Company in a take-private deal in late 2021, valued at about $1.3 billion, and later merged into Worldwide Express group. Crunchbase shows about $400 million in funding from 2015. B2B freight brokerage, little consumer awareness.

Avidity Biosciences is a US biotechnology company based in San Diego, developing antibody oligonucleotide conjugates (AOCs) to treat muscle diseases such as myotonic dystrophy type 1, facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy and Duchenne. Its clinical programmes are del-desiran, del-brax and del-zota. It is listed on Nasdaq (RNA). In October 2025 Novartis agreed to acquire Avidity for about $12 billion. The Crunchbase description given refers to an unrelated consulting firm and appears to be a data error. Clinical-stage with no products on the market and no consumer visibility.

Baxter International is a US medical products company based in Deerfield, Illinois, founded in 1931. It makes hospital beds, infusion pumps, IV solutions, renal care and dialysis products, surgical and monitoring equipment and pharmaceuticals, and in 2021 acquired Hillrom. Customers are hospitals, dialysis clinics and healthcare systems in over 100 countries, with about 38,000 employees and revenue of roughly $10-11 billion. Kidney care was sold as Vantive to Carlyle in 2025. Listed on the NYSE under BAX. B2B healthcare brand with low consumer visibility.

Biohaven is a US biopharmaceutical company based in New Haven, Connecticut, developing treatments for neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases, including troriluzole for spinocerebellar ataxia, taldefgrobep alfa for spinal muscular atrophy and degraders for immune disorders. This is the 2022 spin-off of the earlier Biohaven Pharmaceuticals, whose migraine drug Nurtec ODT was bought by Pfizer for $11.6 billion in 2022. Customers will be neurologists and patients. It has no commercial revenue yet and is listed on the NYSE (BHVN). No consumer brand profile.

BioNTech is a German biotechnology company based in Mainz, founded in 2008 by Ugur Sahin and Ozlem Tureci. It co-developed the Comirnaty mRNA COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer, and now focuses on cancer immunotherapies, mRNA, antibodies and cell therapies, acquiring CureVac in 2025 and licensing a PD-L1xVEGF antibody from Biotheus. Customers are governments, health systems and pharma partners, with revenue falling from the pandemic peak. About 7,000 employees. Listed on Nasdaq (BNTX). Highly recognised name from the pandemic, but little consumer advertising.

Braskem is Latin America's largest petrochemical company and a leading producer of biopolymers, headquartered in Sao Paulo. It makes polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC and green polyethylene from sugarcane ethanol, with plants in Brazil, the US, Mexico and Germany, and sells resins to plastics converters in packaging, automotive and construction. Revenue is around $15-20 billion. Controlled by Novonor (formerly Odebrecht) and Petrobras, and listed on B3 (BRKM5) and the NYSE (BAK). Pure B2B brand, though Braskem has appeared in Brazilian sports sponsorship.

Collegium Pharmaceutical is a US specialty pharma company based in Stoughton, Massachusetts, marketing pain medicines including Xtampza ER, Nucynta, Belbuca and Symproic, and acquired Ironshore, with a focus on abuse-deterrent formulations. Customers are pain specialists, pharmacies and payers in the United States. Revenue is around $700 million. Listed on Nasdaq under COLL. B2B pharma brand, with no consumer profile, and a restricted category for marketing.

Convatec is a UK medical products company based in London, developing and selling advanced wound dressings, ostomy and continence care products, critical care devices and infusion pumps for diabetes. Brands include Aquacel, Natura, Esteem and Flexi-Seal. Customers are hospitals, healthcare systems, clinicians and patients, with sales in over 100 countries, revenue of roughly $2.3 billion and about 10,000 employees. Founded in 1978 as part of Bristol-Myers Squibb, it was later owned by private equity and listed on the London Stock Exchange in 2016 (CTEC), a FTSE 100 member. Little consumer awareness.

Corteva Agriscience is a US agricultural company based in Indianapolis, created in 2019 when DowDuPont split its agriculture arm. It sells corn and soybean seeds under the Pioneer and Brevant brands, and crop protection products such as herbicides, insecticides and biologicals, to farmers and distributors in over 140 countries. Revenue is around $16-17 billion. Listed on the NYSE under CTVA, and in 2025 it announced plans to separate its seed and crop protection businesses. Strong brand with farmers, almost no consumer awareness.

Diversified Healthcare Trust is a US real estate investment trust headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, managed by The RMR Group. It owns senior living communities, medical office buildings and life science properties across the United States, earning rental income and resident fees from operators and tenants. It was formed from the 2019 merger of Senior Housing Properties Trust and Government Properties Income Trust. Listed on Nasdaq under DHC. Balance-sheet heavy and financially stretched. B2B property investor with no consumer brand visibility.

Gevo is a US renewable fuels company based in Englewood, Colorado, developing sustainable aviation fuel and renewable gasoline from ethanol and isobutanol made from corn and other feedstocks. It is working on alcohol-to-jet production at its Net-Zero projects in North Dakota and South Dakota, and acquired the Red Trail Energy ethanol and carbon capture plant in 2024. Customers are airlines, fuel distributors and corporate buyers of low-carbon fuel. Listed on Nasdaq under GEVO, with limited revenue to date. Visible in clean energy circles, little consumer awareness.

Grail is a US healthcare company based in Menlo Park, California, that sells the Galleri blood test, a multi-cancer early detection screening test that looks for a cancer signal across more than 50 cancer types. Customers are consumers who pay via physicians, health systems and employers, with NHS England testing a large trial. It was founded by Illumina in 2016, spun out as a public company in June 2024, and trades on Nasdaq as GRAL. Still loss-making, with modest revenue. Reasonable public profile in health news.

Guardant Health is a US precision oncology company based in Palo Alto, California, founded in 2012. It sells blood-based tests including Guardant360 and Guardant Reveal for cancer therapy selection and recurrence monitoring, and Shield, an FDA-approved blood test for colorectal cancer screening. Customers are oncologists, hospitals, pharma companies and health systems. Revenue is above $700 million, and it is listed on Nasdaq under GH. B2B and healthcare provider brand, with limited but growing awareness among patients.

Immunovant is a clinical-stage US biopharmaceutical company, based in New York, developing antibodies that target the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn) for autoimmune diseases such as myasthenia gravis, thyroid eye disease and Graves' disease. Pipeline assets include batoclimab and IMVT-1402. It is a majority-owned subsidiary of Roivant Sciences and is listed on Nasdaq under IMVT. It has no marketed products yet and earns no product revenue. B2B biotech with essentially no consumer brand awareness.

J.B. Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals is an Indian drug maker based in Mumbai that makes branded generics and contract manufactured formulations. Its brands include Rantac, Metrogyl, Cilacar and Nicardia, sold to Indian doctors and pharmacies, in addition to exports and CDMO work. In 2020 the investor KKR bought control, and in 2025 Torrent Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire a controlling stake. Listed on the NSE and BSE under JBCHEPHARM. Familiar to Indian doctors and pharmacies, but moderate public brand awareness.

John Deere (Deere & Company) is the world's largest agricultural machinery maker, based in Moline, Illinois, founded in 1837. It sells tractors, combines, sprayers, construction and forestry equipment and lawn and turf products, plus precision agriculture technology and John Deere Financial, to farmers, contractors and dealers worldwide. Revenue is around $45-55 billion depending on the year. Listed on the NYSE under DE. The green-and-yellow brand is a household name in the US and in rural markets, with a strong global dealer network.

Kymera Therapeutics is a US clinical-stage biotech based in Watertown, Massachusetts, developing targeted protein degraders, small molecules that remove disease-causing proteins. Its lead programme KT-621 targets STAT6 for allergic and inflammatory diseases, and it has collaborations with Sanofi, Vertex and Gilead. Revenue comes from partnership payments rather than product sales. Listed on Nasdaq under KYMR. B2B drug developer with no consumer brand profile.

Lenta is a major Russian food retailer, founded in St. Petersburg in 1993 and operating hypermarkets and supermarkets in cities across Russia, selling groceries and general goods to consumers. It bought the Billa Russia supermarket chain in 2020 and has revenue in the hundreds of billions of roubles. It was listed in London through GDRs and in Moscow, and was later redomiciled to Russia and listed on the Moscow Exchange (LENT). Controlled by Severgroup, linked to Alexey Mordashov. Strong consumer brand in Russia, subject to sanctions-related restrictions.

Madrigal Pharmaceuticals is a US biopharmaceutical company based in Conshohocken, Pennsylvania. Its product Rezdiffra (resmetirom), approved by the US FDA in March 2024 and in Europe in 2025, is the first approved medicine for non-alcoholic steatohepatitis with liver fibrosis (MASH). Customers are hepatologists, gastroenterologists, payers and patients. Sales are growing rapidly from launch. Listed on Nasdaq under MDGL. Small company with strong investor interest, low consumer awareness.

Nuvalent is a US clinical-stage oncology biotech based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, developing kinase inhibitors for lung cancer patients with ALK or ROS1 alterations, including zidesamtinib and neladalkib. The company is preparing to bring its first drugs to market following pivotal data and regulatory filings. It earns no product revenue yet and is funded through public offerings. Listed on Nasdaq under NUVL. Highly valued by investors but with no consumer brand profile.

Quinn Residences is a real estate company in the Commercial Real Estate sector, with Crunchbase showing an Atlanta, Georgia location and an entry that begins with providing residential-related real estate services. Total funding is shown as $2.75 billion, latest in November 2024. The scale, owners, properties and customers cannot be confirmed from the input, and the size of the funding figure suggests a platform-type fund or investment programme rather than an operating brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Structure Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharma company with offices in South San Francisco and Shanghai, developing oral small-molecule drugs for obesity and metabolic diseases. Its lead candidate aleniglipron (GSBR-1290) is an oral GLP-1 receptor agonist in Phase 2 and later trials. It has no marketed products and is funded by equity raises, including a large 2025 offering. Listed on Nasdaq as GPCR via ADSs. B2B biotech with no consumer brand visibility.

Suzano is a Brazilian pulp and paper company headquartered in Sao Paulo, the world's largest producer of market eucalyptus pulp after its 2019 merger with Fibria. It also sells paper, packaging board and consumer tissue under brands such as Report and Neve, and moved into the international tissue business with Kimberly-Clark in 2025. Customers are tissue, paper and packaging manufacturers worldwide, mainly in China, Europe and North America. Controlled by the Feffer family and listed on B3 (SUZB3) and NYSE (SUZ). Largely B2B, with some Brazilian consumer brands.

Takeda is Japan's largest pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Tokyo and founded in 1781. It sells prescription medicines in gastroenterology (Entyvio), rare diseases, plasma-derived therapies, oncology and neuroscience (Vyvanse), after acquiring Shire in 2019, with operations in around 80 countries and revenue of more than 4 trillion yen. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4502) and the NYSE (TAK). Well-known corporate brand but little consumer advertising.

Universal Corporation is a US leaf tobacco supplier based in Richmond, Virginia, buying, processing and selling tobacco to cigarette manufacturers, and expanding into plant-based ingredients through its FruitSmart and Silva divisions. Major customers are global tobacco companies, and it has operations in Brazil, Africa, Asia and Europe. Revenue is about $2.5-3 billion. Listed on the NYSE under UVV. Pure B2B agricultural supplier, with no consumer brand, and tobacco-related restrictions on sponsorship.

Dazhong Dianping is China's pioneering local lifestyle review and discovery platform, founded in Shanghai in 2003, where consumers read reviews and book restaurants, hotels and services. It received investment from Tencent, and in 2015 merged with Meituan to form Meituan-Dianping, now Meituan, which is listed in Hong Kong (3690). Dianping continues as an app inside Meituan, with revenue from advertising and merchant services. Crunchbase shows $1.16 billion raised by 2015. Huge consumer awareness in China, no international presence.

Dream Sports is an Indian sports technology company based in Mumbai, founded in 2008 by Harsh Jain and Bhavit Sheth. It owns Dream11, India's largest fantasy sports platform with a claimed 200 million users, along with FanCode (sports streaming and merchandise), DreamSetGo (sports experiences) and Dream Capital. Dream11 was India's lead cricket jersey sponsor. Very high consumer awareness.

Dream11 is India's largest fantasy sports app, operated by Dream Sports from Mumbai. India banned real-money online gaming in August 2025, ending its core business model. Exceptional Indian consumer brand awareness and a proven sports sponsor.

Greystar CPP U.S. Build-for-Rent JV is a joint venture between Greystar, the global rental housing manager and developer, and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPP Investments), formed to develop single-family and townhome build-for-rent communities in the United States. It is an investment vehicle rather than an operating brand, with funding of about $1.47 billion shown in August 2025. Customers are renters, and revenue is rental income. Greystar is based in Charleston, South Carolina. Low consumer visibility for the JV itself.

Silicon Motion Technology is a Taiwanese fabless semiconductor company, based in Hsinchu, designing NAND flash controllers for SSDs, eMMC and UFS and SD cards, plus MonTitan enterprise SSD solutions. Customers are flash makers and storage brands such as Samsung, Micron, Kioxia and SK Hynix. Its ADSs are listed on Nasdaq (SIMO). A planned 2023 acquisition by MaxLinear was terminated. Revenue is around $500-800 million. B2B chip supplier with little consumer brand awareness.

TAB is a company in Commercial Real Estate that provides short-term bridging loans for property, with its location shown in Borehamwood, Hertfordshire, United Kingdom. Crunchbase shows about 920 million in funding, last event in September 2025. It cannot be confirmed from the input how large it is, who owns it or what products it offers beyond bridging finance. B2B property lender with no known consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

The Access Group is a UK business management software company based in Loughborough, Leicestershire, founded in 1991. It sells cloud software for finance, HR and payroll, supply chain, hospitality, health and care, education and nonprofit sectors to roughly 100,000 customers, mainly in the UK, Ireland, Australia and the US, and has grown through more than 100 acquisitions. Revenue exceeds GBP 1 billion. Owned by private equity investors Hg, TA Associates and Ontario Teachers'. Mostly B2B, but active in sports and events sponsorship.

ASE Technology Holding is the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, based in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, formed in 2018 from Advanced Semiconductor Engineering and Siliconware Precision Industries. It offers chip packaging, testing, advanced packaging, electronic manufacturing services and modules, for chipmakers and fabless firms including Apple suppliers, with revenue above $18 billion. Listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (3711) and NYSE (ASX). B2B supplier with very little consumer brand recognition.

CAR Inc. is China's largest car rental company, based in Beijing, and part of the UCAR group founded by Charles Lu in 2007. It rents cars with and without drivers, sells used cars and offers fleet leasing, and is the Chinese master licensee of Hertz in China. Customers are business and leisure users in Chinese cities and airports. It was listed in Hong Kong in 2014 (0699), with Crunchbase showing about $904 million raised. Moderately known in China as a travel and mobility brand.

European Energy is a Danish developer of wind, solar and power-to-X projects, based in Soborg near Copenhagen and founded in 2004. It develops, builds, owns and operates renewable parks in Europe, the US, Latin America and Australia, and sells electricity and sells projects to investors, and it is building e-methanol production at Kasso in Denmark. Employees are around 700-1,000. Crunchbase shows about $939 million in funding in August 2026. B2B energy company with limited consumer awareness.

Fertiglobe is the world's largest seaborne exporter of nitrogen fertilizers, based in Abu Dhabi. It produces urea, ammonia and other products at plants in the UAE, Egypt and Algeria, and sells to farmers and distributors in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas. ADNOC owns a majority stake of 86 percent, with OCI previously the majority holder before selling in 2023. Listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange (FERTIGLB). B2B commodity producer with minimal consumer visibility.

Mater Private Hospital is a private Catholic hospital in Dublin, Ireland, part of the Mater Private Network, offering cardiac care, cancer treatment, emergency medicine, orthopaedics and diagnostics to patients covered by private health insurance or self-paying. Crunchbase shows about 820 million in funding in September 2026. Customers are Irish private patients and insurers, and it is one of the larger private hospitals in the country. Local healthcare brand in Ireland, with moderate recognition among Irish consumers and none elsewhere.

Medicover is an international healthcare and diagnostics group headquartered in Stockholm, founded in 1995, that runs clinics, hospitals, dentistry, laboratory diagnostics and prepaid health plans mainly in Poland, Germany, Romania, Ukraine and India. Customers include corporate employers who buy healthcare packages, private patients and public payers, with revenue above EUR 2 billion and over 40,000 staff. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (MCOV B). Strong brand in Poland and Central Europe, almost none elsewhere.

NEPI Rockcastle is the largest listed owner of shopping centres in Central and Eastern Europe, with about 60 malls in Romania, Poland, Slovakia, Hungary, Czechia, Bulgaria and Croatia and retail properties valued at roughly EUR 7-8 billion. Tenants are fashion, food and entertainment retailers, and income is rent. Headquartered in Bucharest with a legal base in the Isle of Man, later moved to the Netherlands. Listed on Johannesburg, Euronext Amsterdam and Bucharest exchanges (NRP). Mall brands are known locally, while the owner is a B2B landlord.

Unitel is Angola's largest mobile telecoms operator, based in Luanda, launched in 2001. It serves roughly 13-15 million mobile customers with voice, data and mobile money, and also has interests outside Angola such as in Cape Verde and Sao Tome. Ownership has involved Angolan state-linked and private investors, with a long-running public dispute over stakes tied to Isabel dos Santos. Customers are consumers and businesses across Angola. It is one of the best-known Angolan consumer brands and an active sports and culture sponsor, though confined to one national market.

Vista Land & Lifescapes is a Philippine property developer controlled by the Villar family and listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (VLL). It builds and sells homes through brands such as Camella, Crown Asia, Brittany and Vista Residences, and operates Vistamalls shopping centres. Customers are Filipino homebuyers across the mass, middle and premium segments, plus mall tenants. It is headquartered in Metro Manila and runs hundreds of residential communities nationwide. Strong brand visibility among Filipino consumers, little elsewhere.

Zhenkunxing (Zkh) is a Chinese industrial supplies platform based in Shanghai, selling maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) products to manufacturers, such as tools, safety equipment, bearings and consumables, through online ordering, warehouses and its own brands. Customers are Chinese industrial firms of all sizes, and it earns product sales. Backed by investors such as Alibaba, Tiger Global and Sequoia China; Crunchbase shows about $1 billion in funding by June 2022. B2B brand, low consumer awareness.

Acciona Energia is a Spanish renewable energy company based in Madrid, developing, building and operating wind, solar, hydro and storage assets in Spain, the US, Mexico, Chile, Australia and elsewhere, with about 13-14 GW of installed capacity. It sells electricity to utilities, industrial customers and retail consumers. Acciona SA holds about 80 percent, and the shares are listed on the Spanish stock exchange (ANE) since 2021. Acciona group sponsors sport events, but Acciona Energia itself has limited consumer awareness.

Aedifica is a Belgian real estate investment trust based in Brussels that owns care homes, senior housing and healthcare properties across Belgium, the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Finland, Sweden, Ireland and Spain, leasing them to care operators on long leases. Portfolio value is about EUR 6 billion. It is listed on Euronext Brussels (AED), with a secondary listing in Amsterdam. B2B property investor with no consumer brand profile.

Alorica is a US business process outsourcing company, based in Irvine, California, that provides customer service, technical support, sales and back-office outsourcing through contact centres and remote agents across North America, Latin America, the Philippines and Europe. Customers are large corporations in telecoms, retail, technology and financial services. It employs tens of thousands of people and generates over $2 billion in revenue. Privately held. B2B service provider with limited public brand awareness.

Anglian Water Services is the main water and wastewater utility for the East of England, based in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire. It supplies drinking water to millions of households and businesses and handles wastewater across the largest geographic area of any English water company. It is regulated by Ofwat and is part of Anglian Water Group, owned by a consortium of infrastructure investors including CPP Investments, IFM and Ontario Teachers'. Regional consumer-facing utility with strong local visibility and community partnerships in its region.

Ardea Resources is an Australian mineral exploration and development company based in Perth, focused on nickel and cobalt in Western Australia, notably the Kalgoorlie Nickel Project, plus gold and critical minerals tenements. It is a pre-production developer with no significant revenue, funded by equity raisings, and listed on the ASX under ARL. Customers will be battery and stainless steel supply chains. B2B resources developer with little public awareness.

Aster DM Healthcare is a healthcare group founded by Dr Azad Moopen in 1987, headquartered in Dubai. It operates hospitals, clinics and retail pharmacies across the GCC under Aster, Medcare and Access brands, and in India through Aster hospitals, serving patients and insurers. Its structure was split between a Gulf business and an Indian business, listed on the NSE and BSE as Aster DM Healthcare. Revenue is over $1 billion. Familiar healthcare brand in the UAE, Saudi Arabia and Kerala, with limited global profile.

Atlantic Alumina (Atalco) operates an alumina refinery at Gramercy, Louisiana, converting imported bauxite into alumina that is sold to aluminium smelters and to chemical customers. It is a privately owned industrial producer, and Crunchbase shows $800 million in funding, latest in August 2026. Customers are metal and chemical manufacturers, and revenue comes from tonnage sold. The scale and ownership structure cannot be fully confirmed from the input. B2B industrial minerals business with no consumer brand profile.

Atome Energy is a UK-headquartered developer of low-carbon fertilizer and green hydrogen projects, based in Leeds, with its flagship Villeta project in Paraguay planned to produce ammonia and nitrate fertilizer using renewable hydroelectric power. Customers would be agricultural fertilizer buyers and industrial users. It has no significant revenue yet and is listed (formerly as Atome Plc on the London AIM market). Crunchbase shows about $867 million in funding, latest in April 2026. B2B project developer, no consumer visibility.

Cambria Gold Mines is a Canadian mining company based in Vancouver, British Columbia, described in the input as a mineral development business. Crunchbase shows about $731 million in funding, latest event in October 2026, though that figure looks large for a development-stage company and may relate to a project financing. Its assets, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed from the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Canada Nickel Company is a Canadian mining developer based in Toronto, building the Crawford nickel-cobalt sulphide project near Timmins, Ontario, one of the largest undeveloped nickel deposits in the world, with a planned low-carbon nickel mine and processing. Led by Mark Selby, it sells nothing yet and is raising project funding with support from Canadian government programmes and strategic investors including Agnico Eagle. Listed on the TSX Venture Exchange (CNC). B2B resources developer with low public profile.

CenterNode is a Los Angeles-based company described by Crunchbase as a recently launched alternative energy business, with about $750 million in funding shown for April 2026. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Clearway Energy is a US owner of contracted renewable and conventional power assets, based in Princeton, New Jersey, with about 12 GW of wind, solar, storage and thermal capacity and thermal steam and chilled water systems. It sells electricity under long-term contracts to utilities and corporate offtakers. It is sponsored by TotalEnergies and Global Infrastructure Partners (BlackRock) and listed on the NYSE (CWEN, CWEN.A). B2B yieldco with no consumer brand profile.

EQUATE Petrochemical Company is a Kuwaiti petrochemical producer, based in Safat, Kuwait, making ethylene glycol and polyethylene from facilities at Shuaiba and operating the TKOC unit. It is a joint venture of Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC), Dow, Boubyan Petrochemical and Gulf Investment Corporation, selling to plastics and packaging manufacturers in Asia, Europe and the Middle East. It is a large industrial exporter with annual capacity in the millions of tonnes. B2B chemical supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Franklin Resources is a global asset manager based in San Mateo, California, operating as Franklin Templeton, with brands including Templeton, Legg Mason affiliates (acquired 2020), Clarion Partners, Martin Currie and Western Asset. It manages about $1.5-1.6 trillion for retail investors, institutions and sovereign funds in more than 150 countries and employs about 9,000 people. Revenue comes from management fees. Listed on the NYSE as BEN, with the Johnson family as major shareholders. Well known in finance and active in sports and events marketing.

Grupo EcoRodovias is a Brazilian infrastructure and logistics group, with a base in the Sao Paulo area, that operates toll road concessions in several states and port logistics in Santos through Ecoporto. Customers are motorists and cargo operators, and revenue comes from toll fees and logistics services. It was controlled by Italian group Gavio and then by Argo Infrastructure Partners after 2022. Crunchbase shows BRL 4.2 billion funding in July 2022. Familiar to Brazilian road users, but not a national consumer brand.

Hecla Mining is the oldest US-listed precious metals miner, founded in 1891 in Idaho and headquartered in Coeur d'Alene, although Crunchbase shows a Nevada location (Hollister mine). It is the largest US silver producer, operating Greens Creek in Alaska, Lucky Friday in Idaho, Keno Hill in Yukon and Casa Berardi in Quebec, and sells silver and gold concentrates and doré to smelters and refiners. Listed on the NYSE under HL. B2B commodity producer, little consumer awareness.

Hill Group UK is a family-owned housebuilder and developer based in Waltham Abbey, Essex, building private homes, affordable housing and mixed-use regeneration schemes across London and the South East of England. It sells to homebuyers, housing associations and local authorities, completing several hundred to over a thousand homes a year. Crunchbase shows GBP 500 million in funding in January 2026. Regional residential brand with local recognition, and little national consumer awareness.

Hubei Xingchen is a company based in Wuhan, Hubei, China, whose Crunchbase description says it focuses on an unspecified field. Incoco Charney Tavros JV is a joint venture firm headquartered in New York, with Crunchbase showing $785 million in funding in June 2026. Indivior is a specialty pharmaceutical company focused on treatments for opioid use disorder, with Sublocade, Suboxone film and Opvee (nasal opioid overdose reversal). Customers are doctors, addiction clinics, pharmacies, payers and patients, with revenue of roughly $1 billion, mostly in the US. Listed on Nasdaq (INDV) and the LSE. Known in healthcare, not a consumer brand.

Kenter Groendus is a Dutch company based in Utrecht, described as a commercial energy transition business. Crunchbase shows EUR 662 million in funding, latest in October 2026. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

LifeStance Health is the largest US outpatient mental health provider, based in Scottsdale, Arizona, employing thousands of psychiatrists, psychologists, therapists and nurse practitioners at roughly 600 centres in over 30 states, delivering in-person and telehealth care. Revenue comes from insurers and patients, and is above $1.2 billion a year. Founded in 2017, it is backed by Summit Partners and TPG and listed on Nasdaq (LFST). Local clinic brand with moderate national consumer awareness.

Naver Financial is the financial services subsidiary of South Korean internet group Naver, based in Seongnam. It runs Naver Pay, a leading online and mobile payment service used across Naver Shopping and offline merchants, plus lending, insurance comparison, securities and Naver Pay point services. In 2025 it announced a deal to combine with Dunamu, operator of the Upbit crypto exchange, through a share swap. Crunchbase shows a large funding total of KRW 800 billion from 2019. Very high awareness in Korea, small outside it.

Oerlikon is a Swiss industrial technology group based in Pfaffikon, with two main divisions: Surface Solutions, which applies coatings to tools and automotive and aerospace parts, and Polymer Processing Solutions (Barmag), which makes equipment for man-made fibres. Customers are industrial manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, tooling and textiles in over 35 countries, with revenue of about CHF 2.4 billion. Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (OERL). The name is historic but largely B2B, with little consumer awareness.

OPAP is the Greek national lottery and betting operator, based in Athens and founded in 1958, running lotteries, Tzoker, Kino, sports betting with Stoiximan and Pamestoixima, and online games with Betano, plus VLTs. In 2024-2025 it combined with Allwyn, the Czech-based lottery group of Karel Komarek, and has been renamed Allwyn Hellas under Allwyn's ownership. Customers are Greek consumers through thousands of retail agencies and online. Listed on Athens Exchange. Very high Greek consumer awareness and a long sponsor of Greek football and basketball.

Option Care Health is the largest independent home and alternate-site infusion services provider in the United States, formed in 2019 through the merger of BioScrip and Option Care. It delivers infused and injected medicines and nutrition therapy to patients at home or in infusion suites, with revenue near $5 billion, covering all states. Customers are patients, physicians, hospitals and insurers. Listed on Nasdaq (OPCH). Healthcare services brand with low consumer awareness.

Sandisk is a leading US flash memory and storage brand, based in Milpitas, California, founded in 1988 and spun off from Western Digital in February 2025 as a separate company listed on Nasdaq (SNDK). It makes NAND flash memory, SSDs and consumer products such as SanDisk SD cards, USB drives and portable SSDs, sold through retailers and to data centre and device customers. Revenue is about $7 billion. Joint venture with Kioxia manufactures wafers in Japan. A very recognisable consumer storage brand worldwide.

SellerX was a Berlin-based e-commerce aggregator founded in 2020 by Philipp Triebel and Malte Horeyseck, which bought and scaled third-party brands selling on Amazon, in categories such as home, baby and outdoor. It raised more than $800 million in equity and debt and acquired dozens of brands in Europe and the US, then restructured in 2023 after the aggregator model faltered and cut jobs and brands. Customers are consumers buying via Amazon. Brand is known in the startup community, not to consumers.

Serra Verde is a Brazilian rare earths producer based in Goias, operating the Pela Ema ionic clay project, one of the few sources of heavy and light rare earths outside China. It supplies concentrate for magnets used in electric vehicles and wind turbines, with backing from investors such as Denham Capital and Vision Blue and financing from the US DFC. Customers are magnet makers and processors. Private company. B2B critical minerals business with no consumer brand profile.

Shandong Hengsheng Graphite Technology is a machinery and materials manufacturer based in Jining, Shandong, China. The Crunchbase line says it is a graphite company, and funding is shown as CNY 5 billion in September 2023. Details of its products, customers, ownership and scale are not given in the input, so they cannot be confirmed. Likely a B2B industrial supplier. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Sharecare is a US digital health and wellness company, based in Atlanta, offering an app and platform for consumers, employers, health plans and hospitals. It provides health content, programmes, a care management service and the Sharecare app, and was co-founded in 2010 by Jeff Arnold and Dr Oz. It listed on Nasdaq through a SPAC (SHCR) in 2021 and was acquired by Altaris in 2024 in a take-private deal worth about $518 million. Moderately known in US health and wellness circles.

Stanley Black & Decker is a US tools and industrial company, based in New Britain, Connecticut, formed in 2010 by the merger of Stanley Works and Black & Decker. It makes hand tools, power tools and outdoor products under DeWalt, Craftsman, Stanley, Black+Decker and Cub Cadet, and sells to consumers through retailers such as Home Depot and Lowe's, as well as industrial and construction customers. Revenue is about $15 billion and it has operations worldwide. Listed on the NYSE (SWK). Very strong consumer and trades brand awareness.

Syrah Resources is an Australian natural graphite and battery materials company, based in Melbourne, operating the Balama graphite mine in Mozambique and the Vidalia active anode material plant in Louisiana. It sells graphite and battery anode material to EV and battery makers, notably Tesla. It is listed on the ASX (SYR) and has been hit by weak graphite prices. B2B materials supplier with little consumer awareness.

Technopolis is a Finnish provider of office space, innovation campuses and business services for technology and growth companies, with roots in Oulu from 1982. It leases flexible offices and co-working to tenants in Finland, Estonia, Norway, Lithuania and Russia, and was formerly listed on Nasdaq Helsinki before being taken private by Keva-backed investors. The input describes it as privately held. B2B real estate and workplace brand with limited consumer awareness.

VAST is an artificial intelligence company working on generative AI for 3D content, based in Hong Kong with a research team in China, and creator of the Tripo family of tools that turn text or images into 3D models. Customers are game developers, designers, e-commerce sellers and makers. The company was founded in 2023 by Song-Hai Zhang, a former Tsinghua University researcher. Crunchbase shows about $844 million in funding by September 2026. Developer-focused brand, little mainstream awareness.

VeraDermics is a US dermatology company based in New Haven, Connecticut, developing prescription treatments for hair loss, with a lead candidate for pattern hair loss, a new extended-release oral therapy. It has no marketed products and is funded by venture and public equity, with about $733 million shown by April 2026. Customers will be dermatologists and patients. Little consumer awareness yet, though hair loss is a large consumer market.

Vizsla Silver is a Canadian exploration and development company based in Vancouver, advancing the Panuco silver-gold project in Sinaloa, Mexico, which holds a large silver resource. It has no production or revenue and is funded by equity raises. Listed on NYSE American and TSX under VZLA. B2B resource developer with no consumer brand profile. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Wanguo International Mining Group is a mining company based in China, listed in Hong Kong according to the listed flag, operating mines in the industrial and metals sector. B2B commodity producer with no consumer profile. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

WildBlue Communications was a US satellite broadband provider, founded in 2001 and based in Colorado, offering high-speed satellite internet to rural households and small businesses in the US, using Ka-band capacity from Telesat and its own satellites. It was acquired by ViaSat in late 2009 for about $568 million and later rebranded as Exede, now Viasat internet. Crunchbase shows $693 million in funding by 2008. No longer an independent brand.

Worthington Steel is a US flat-rolled steel processor based in Columbus, Ohio, spun off from Worthington Enterprises in December 2023. It processes carbon, galvanized and electrical steels into coils and sheets, with toll processing for customers in automotive, construction, agriculture, heavy truck and energy markets, at about 40 facilities in the US, Canada, Mexico and elsewhere. Revenue is about $3 billion. Listed on the NYSE (WS). B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Zain Group is a Kuwait-based mobile telecoms group with operations in Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Jordan, Bahrain and Sudan, serving about 50 million customers with voice, data, fibre, 5G and enterprise services. It started as MTC in Kuwait and later expanded across Africa, then sold African businesses. Listed on the Boursa Kuwait (ZAIN), with large shareholders including Kuwait's Public Institution for Social Security. Strong consumer brand across the Gulf and a prominent sports and events sponsor in the region.

Advanced Petrochemical Company is a Saudi chemicals producer based in Jubail, listed on Tadawul (2330). It runs a propane dehydrogenation unit making propylene and polypropylene, and supplies petrochemical products and related industrial gases and utilities to plastics converters and industrial customers in Saudi Arabia and export markets. Founded in 2003 and controlled by Saudi industrial investors. Crunchbase shows SAR 2.2 billion in funding as read. B2B petrochemical supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Allied Gold is a Canadian gold miner based in Toronto, with producing mines in Africa, namely Sadiola in Mali and Bonikro in Cote d'Ivoire, and the Kurmuk project in Ethiopia. It sells gold doré to refiners and earns revenue from ounces sold, typically in the hundreds of thousands of ounces a year. The company listed on the TSX and NYSE (AAUC / AU) in 2023, with Crunchbase showing about $628 million in funding by July 2026. B2B commodity miner with no consumer visibility.

Almoosa Specialist Hospital is a private hospital and healthcare group based in Hofuf, in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province, offering specialist surgical, maternity, cardiac and oncology care to patients in Al Ahsa and nearby cities, with several hospitals and clinics. It was founded in 2008 and is listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul) after its 2025 IPO. Crunchbase shows SAR 2.49 billion in funding in July 2026. Strong regional brand in the Eastern Province, but no national or international consumer profile.

Cornish Metals is a UK mineral development company, based in Truro, Cornwall, advancing the South Crofty tin mine and the Redmoor tin-tungsten project, with the aim of restarting tin production in Europe. The company has no production revenue, and has attracted financing including UK government-backed export finance for the South Crofty restart. Listed on the TSX Venture and London AIM (CUSN). Pre-production resource business with limited consumer awareness but a high regional profile in Cornwall.

Encompass Health is a US post-acute care provider based in Birmingham, Alabama, formerly HealthSouth. It operates about 160 inpatient rehabilitation hospitals in 40 states and Puerto Rico, treating stroke, brain injury, hip fracture and other patients, with revenue of around $5 billion and Medicare as the largest payer. It spun off its home health and hospice business as Enhabit in 2022. Listed on the NYSE (EHC). Well-known local hospital brand, though not a national consumer name.

Euro Sun Mining is a Canadian exploration and development company, based in Toronto, with the Rovina Valley gold and copper project in Romania as its main asset. B2B resource developer with no consumer awareness.

FajarPaper is the trading name of Fajar Surya Wisesa, an Indonesian manufacturer of packaging paper, such as kraft liner and corrugating medium, with mills near Jakarta. It sells to corrugated box makers serving food, consumer goods and e-commerce customers. The company is listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange and is based in Jakarta. Crunchbase shows about $652 million in funding. B2B industrial supplier with no consumer brand profile.

Generation Mining is a Canadian mineral development company based in Toronto, advancing the Marathon palladium-copper project in northwestern Ontario, which is permitted and seeking project financing. Global Atomic Corporation is a Canadian company based in Toronto, developing the Dasa uranium project in Niger and operating a zinc oxide recycling facility in Turkey through its Befesa Silvermet Turkey joint venture. It plans to sell uranium to nuclear utilities, and zinc oxide to metal buyers. Listed on the TSX (GLO) and OTCQX. Funding to date includes a large Dasa project financing, with Crunchbase showing $673 million by September 2026. B2B resource company with no consumer visibility.

Greatland is a gold and copper company founded in London, which discovered the Havieron deposit with Newcrest and bought the Telfer mine and surrounding assets in Western Australia from Newcrest (now Newmont) in 2024. It sells gold and copper concentrate, and now operates as Greatland Resources, with its main listing moving to the ASX alongside London AIM. Crunchbase shows about $605 million in funding. B2B miner, little consumer visibility.

HistoSonics is a US medical device company based in Plymouth, Minnesota, that makes the Edison system, a non-invasive focused ultrasound platform for histotripsy, which mechanically destroys liver tumours, with FDA clearance in 2023.
