Kopi Kenangan is an Indonesian coffee chain, based in Jakarta, founded in 2017 by Edy Tjahyadi and James Prananto, selling grab-and-go coffee, iced milk coffee and snacks through over 1,000 outlets and delivery apps. It raised a $96 million Series C in December 2021 at a valuation of about $1 billion, with investors including Alpha JWC and Sequoia India. It has expanded across Indonesia with an extensive store network. Strong consumer brand in Indonesia, little recognition elsewhere.

LaunchDarkly is a US software company, based in Oakland, California, whose feature management platform lets engineering teams release, toggle and test software features safely, with experimentation and AI model configuration tools. Customers are thousands of software companies and enterprises, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2014, it raised about $330 million and was valued near $3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B developer brand, with no consumer awareness.

Lexin is a Chinese online consumer finance and e-commerce platform, based in Shenzhen, founded in 2013 as Fenqile, offering instalment financing and installment shopping to young Chinese consumers, with loan facilitation and credit services. It is listed on Nasdaq (LX), where its ADSs trade, and has raised about $345 million in private funding before its 2017 IPO. Customers are mainly young Chinese consumers. Domestic consumer brand recognition.

Lyten is a US battery company, based in San Jose, California, developing lithium-sulfur batteries and 3D graphene materials for electric vehicles, drones, aerospace and defence. In 2025 it agreed to acquire assets of Northvolt in Sweden, Poland and Germany after the Swedish company went bankrupt. It has no mass production yet and has raised more than $360 million in funding. Customers are automakers, aerospace and defence buyers. B2B technology developer with little consumer awareness.

Mercury Financial is a US consumer credit company, based in Atlanta, Georgia (the entry lists the country as Georgia, which refers to the US state), that issues the Mercury Mastercard credit cards to people with fair credit and builds its card services through digital tools. Customers are American consumers who are rebuilding or building credit, and revenue is interest and fees. Funding shown is $339 million in July 2023. Moderate US consumer visibility through direct marketing.

MGT (MGT Consulting) is a US consulting and technology firm based in Tampa, Florida, advising education, government and public sector clients on strategy, education programmes, data and technology implementation. Customers are school districts, universities and public agencies, paying consulting fees. Funding shown is $350 million, latest in December 2025. B2B services firm, with little consumer visibility. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

MOD Pizza is a US fast-casual pizza chain, founded in 2008 in Seattle and based in Bellevue, Washington, offering build-your-own individual pizzas and salads at around 500 restaurants at its peak. It went through a bankruptcy sale in 2024 after financial difficulties, and many sites were closed. Customers are fast-casual diners across the US. Consumer chain with notable awareness in Washington state and the western US.

Molo Finance is a UK digital mortgage platform, based in London, that uses technology to help homebuyers and borrowers apply for mortgages faster, mixing automated underwriting with advice. Customers are UK borrowers, and funding of around 270 million, much of it likely debt, is shown by October 2020. A small challenger in a market dominated by banks. Little mainstream consumer awareness.

Nigerian Breweries is Nigeria's largest and oldest brewer, based in Lagos, founded in 1946. It makes Star, Gulder, Heineken, Legend Extra Stout, Maltina and Amstel Malta, with breweries around the country, selling to distributors and retailers. Heineken N.V. holds about 56 percent. Listed on the Nigerian Exchange (NB) and a major advertiser and sponsor in sport and music. Very high consumer brand awareness in Nigeria, though alcohol marketing is regulated.

Oosto, formerly AnyVision, is an Israeli computer vision company with headquarters shown in New York, offering facial recognition and object recognition software for security, access control and enterprise safety. Customers include governments, airports, casinos and large businesses. It has been backed by SoftBank and Eldridge, with about $352 million raised, and has faced scrutiny over privacy. B2B security technology, with limited consumer awareness.

PatSnap is an intellectual property and innovation intelligence software company, founded in China in 2007 and operating from Singapore, with offices in Shenzhen, the US and Europe. It sells AI-powered patent search, analytics and R&D tools to technology, pharma and industrial firms, universities and law firms. It raised about $350 million, including a $300 million Series E in 2021. B2B software with no consumer awareness.

Quest Software is a US enterprise software company, based in Aliso Viejo, California (shown here as Austin, Texas), selling database management, data protection, IT security and identity tools to large organisations. It was taken private in 2012 by Insight, later bought by Dell, then sold to Francisco Partners and Elliott in 2016, and since 2022 is controlled by Clearlake Capital. Revenue is about $1 billion. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Qumulo is a US enterprise file storage software company, based in Seattle, founded in 2012, whose scale-out file data platform runs on-premises and in public clouds for media, healthcare, research and government customers. It sells subscriptions and raised about $347 million. Privately held. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Qwil is a US fintech company, based in Orlando, Florida, that provides instant payments, a digital wallet and financial tools for independent contractors, freelancers and gig workers, integrating with platform payment systems. Funding shown is $332 million, latest in March 2021, which probably includes debt. Customers are contractors paid via partner platforms. Small B2B2C brand with little consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Redis is a US data technology company, based in Mountain View, California, which commercialises the open-source Redis in-memory database, used for caching, real-time data and AI applications, through Redis Cloud and Redis Enterprise. Customers are developers and enterprises, including large internet companies. It has raised about $357 million, valued at $2 billion in 2021, and has changed its licence several times. B2B developer brand, widely known among software engineers.

SnapLogic is a US enterprise software company, based in San Mateo, California, founded in 2006 by Gaurav Dhillon, whose integration platform as a service (iPaaS) connects applications, data and APIs with a low-code interface and AI agents. Customers are large enterprises, paying subscription fees. It raised about $371 million, including a $165 million round in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, with no consumer awareness.

TechStyle Fashion Group is a US membership-based fashion e-commerce company, based in El Segundo, California, founded by Don Ressler and Adam Goldenberg. Its brands include Fabletics athleisure (co-founded with Kate Hudson), JustFab, ShoeDazzle, FabKids and previously Savage X Fenty with Rihanna, sold online and in retail stores, with revenue over $2 billion. Customers are mostly women who buy via VIP membership. Fabletics has strong consumer brand awareness in the US and Europe. Privately held.

Unqork is a US no-code enterprise application platform, based in New York, founded in 2017 by Gary Hoberman. It lets banks, insurers and governments build complex software with visual tools rather than hand-written code. Customers include large financial firms and public agencies, paying subscriptions. It raised about $365 million, with a valuation of $2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, no consumer awareness.

Vectra AI is a US cybersecurity company, based in San Jose, California, founded in 2011, whose platform uses AI to detect and prioritise attacks across networks, cloud, identity and SaaS (the Attack Signal Intelligence approach). Customers are large enterprises and government agencies, with revenue from subscriptions. It raised about $353 million and was valued at $1.2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

Western Forest Products is a Canadian lumber producer based in Vancouver, with sawmills and timberlands on the coast of British Columbia, selling Douglas fir, hemlock and western red cedar to builders and manufacturers in North America, Japan and China. Revenue is about CAD 1.2 billion. Listed on the TSX (WEF). B2B wood products supplier with no consumer brand profile. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Womai.com is a Chinese business-to-consumer online grocery and healthy food retailer, based in Beijing and launched in 2009 by COFCO (China National Cereals, Oils and Foodstuffs), the state-owned food group. It sells imported and domestic food by home delivery. Crunchbase shows $330 million raised by 2015 from investors. Retail brand tied to a major state-owned food company, with moderate recognition in China.

Workfront was a US enterprise work management software company, based in Lehi, Utah, whose cloud platform helped marketing and creative teams plan and track projects. Customers were large enterprises. Adobe acquired Workfront in December 2020 for about $1.5 billion and it is now part of Adobe Experience Cloud. It raised about $375 million before that. B2B software, no consumer awareness.

Worley is an Australian engineering and professional services group, based in Sydney, delivering design, project management and sustainability services for energy, chemicals and resources customers in around 40 countries. It employs about 50,000 people and has revenue near AUD 12 billion, after acquiring Jacobs' Energy, Chemicals and Resources business in 2019. Listed on the ASX (WOR). B2B engineering brand, with no consumer profile.

Xos Trucks is a US electric commercial vehicle maker, based in Los Angeles, building battery-electric step vans and medium-duty trucks for last-mile delivery fleets, including the StepVan and powertrains. It listed on Nasdaq in 2021 through a SPAC merger (XOS) and has delivered small volumes. Customers include Amazon-type delivery fleets and logistics companies. B2B vehicle brand with limited consumer awareness.

Zenoti is a US cloud software company, based in Bellevue, Washington, founded in 2010, that provides booking, point-of-sale, marketing and management software for salons, spas, medspas and fitness businesses, used at thousands of locations worldwide. It earns subscription and payment fees. Raised about $331 million with a valuation above $1 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, with no consumer awareness.

Vita Group is a UK manufacturer of flexible polyurethane foam and related products, based in Manchester, supplying bedding, furniture, automotive and technical foam products, and part of a wider group with plants in the UK, Europe and elsewhere. Customers are mattress and furniture makers and industrial users. Funding shown is GBP 169 million, latest in April 2025. B2B industrial supplier with little consumer awareness.

Graham Holdings is a US diversified holding company, based in Arlington, Virginia, formerly The Washington Post Company, that owns Kaplan (education), Graham Media Group (local TV stations), Graham Healthcare Group, Hoover Treated Wood Products and Automotive dealerships, among others. Revenue is about $4.5 billion. The Graham family holds control and the stock trades on the NYSE (GHC). Mixed portfolio, with Kaplan and local TV brands visible to consumers.

58 Daojia is a Chinese online home services platform, based in Beijing, spun out of the 58.com classifieds group and founded in 2013, that connects households with cleaners, movers, beauty and repair workers through an app. It raised money from 58.com and other investors, with $300 million shown for September 2020. Customers are Chinese households. Brand awareness in China is moderate, with less reach outside it.

Africa Gateway is an information services company in database and data management, with Crunchbase showing Mumbai, Maharashtra, India as its location and funding of $325 million in December 2021. The input does not make clear whether it is a technology platform or a market intelligence provider, and its customers, ownership and scale cannot be confirmed. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Africa Minerals and Metals Processing (A2MP) is a Dubai-based industrial company that provides platforms and solutions for processing minerals and metals in Africa, according to Crunchbase. Funding of $300 million is shown for November 2025. The input does not say who owns it, which sites it operates or what its output is. B2B industrial business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

AMD Pensando was a US networking and security acceleration company based in Milpitas, California, founded in 2017 by Silicon Valley veterans, building programmable data processing units (DPUs) for cloud and enterprise data centres. AMD completed its acquisition of Pensando in May 2022 for about $1.9 billion, and the products are now part of AMD's data centre line. It raised about $313 million before the deal. B2B chip technology with no consumer brand.

Amentum is a US government and critical infrastructure services contractor, based in Chantilly, Virginia, which merged with Jacobs' Critical Mission Solutions and Cyber & Intelligence businesses in September 2024 and now trades on the NYSE (AMTM). It provides engineering, technical and mission support to the US Department of Defense, NASA, the Department of Energy and allied governments, with revenue around $8-9 billion and about 53,000 employees. B2B brand with no consumer profile.

Amogy is a US clean energy technology company, based in Brooklyn, New York, founded in 2020, which has developed ammonia-to-power systems that crack ammonia into hydrogen to generate electricity for ships, trucks and stationary power. Investors include SK Innovation, Temasek and Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund. It has raised about $313 million. Customers are maritime and heavy industry. Pre-commercial B2B brand, little consumer awareness.

AMSC (American Superconductor) is a US energy technology company, based in Ayer, Massachusetts, founded in 1987, supplying power electronics, grid resilience systems, ship protection systems for the US Navy, and wind turbine control systems and electrical equipment. Customers are utilities, wind turbine makers, the US Navy and semiconductor fabs, with revenue of around $200 million. It is listed on Nasdaq (AMSC). B2B industrial brand with little consumer visibility.

Benefit Street Partners is a US alternative credit manager, based in New York, providing commercial real estate lending, direct lending and private debt for institutions, as well as managing non-traded REITs. It has about $70 billion of assets under management, and since 2019 it has been a part of Franklin Templeton (Legg Mason deal). Customers are institutional investors, borrowers and retail fund investors. B2B finance brand with no consumer awareness.

Billtrust is a US software company, based in Lawrenceville, New Jersey (listed in Nashville, Tennessee), that supplies accounts receivable automation, invoicing and payments software to B2B companies. It listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2021 (BTRS) and was taken private by EQT in early 2022 for around $1.7 billion. Customers include thousands of mid-market and enterprise suppliers. B2B fintech brand with no consumer visibility.

Carplat is a South Korean mobility platform, based in Seongnam, that integrates car rental, leasing and used car services into a platform for retail and business customers. Crunchbase shows a funding of KRW 390 billion in December 2022. Ownership and scale cannot be fully confirmed from the input. Korean consumer-facing mobility brand with limited recognition outside the country. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Chicago Skyway is a 7.8-mile toll road linking the Dan Ryan Expressway to the Indiana Toll Road in Chicago, and was the first US toll road to be leased to private operators in 2005, under a 99-year concession to Skyway Concession Company, then owned by Cintra and Macquarie, and later by new investors. Customers are motorists, who pay tolls. Crunchbase shows $325 million of funding in 2025. Infrastructure asset with no consumer brand beyond local drivers.

Cloudwise is a Chinese AI-driven IT operations and data analytics company, founded in 2009 and shown with a Singapore address, offering full-stack AIOps and big data tools to banks, telecoms, internet and energy enterprises. Customers are large enterprises in China. Crunchbase shows about $315 million raised by July 2021. B2B software with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

commercetools is a German software company, based in Munich, founded in 2004, whose cloud-native, API-first commerce platform helps retailers and brands build online shopping experiences, with customers such as Audi, Danone and Ulta. Revenue comes from subscriptions. Raised about $308 million, with a $1.9 billion valuation in 2021 from investors including REWE and Accel. Privately held. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Digi Communications is a Romanian telecoms group, based in Bucharest, selling mobile, broadband, cable TV and fixed lines under the Digi brand in Romania, Spain, Portugal, Italy and Belgium, with tens of millions of subscriptions. It was founded by Zoltan Teszari, who remains the controlling shareholder, and is listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange (DIGI). Customers are households and businesses. Strong consumer brand in Romania and growing in Spain, with sports TV rights.

DuerOS is Baidu's conversational AI operating system, developed in Beijing, embedded in smart speakers, TVs, cars and appliances to provide voice assistants, and underlies the Xiaodu brand of smart devices. Customers are device makers and consumers. The AI unit later spun into Xiaodu Technology. Funding of CNY 2 billion is shown for September 2020. Strong Chinese consumer device exposure, less outside China.

Everlaw is a US cloud-based eDiscovery and litigation software company, based in Oakland, California, whose platform helps law firms, corporate legal teams and governments review documents and evidence, with AI tools for analysis. Founded in 2010, it raised about $299 million and was valued at over $2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B legal technology brand, no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Extend is a US company, based in San Francisco, offering embedded product protection plans and warranty services to merchants, with an AI-powered commerce platform for protection, claims and post-purchase services. Customers are retailers, such as large online sellers, and shoppers buying warranties. It has raised about $320 million by May 2021. B2B2C brand, with limited consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

FIRY is a Las Vegas, Nevada, company that Crunchbase describes as a founder-led global technology portfolio company, with developer platforms and esports activities, and about $290 million in funding as of December 2020. The input does not tell which brands or products it owns, who its customers are or how large it is. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Hyperscience is a US intelligent document processing company, based in New York, founded in 2014 by Peter Brodsky, whose machine learning platform extracts data from forms, emails and handwritten documents for banks, insurers and governments. Customers are large organisations paying subscriptions. It raised about $289 million, and was valued at over $1 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software brand, no consumer awareness.

Integral Ad Science (IAS) is a US ad verification and measurement company, based in New York, whose technology checks viewability, brand safety and fraud for digital, social and connected TV campaigns, working with advertisers, agencies and publishers globally. Revenue is around $500 million. It listed on Nasdaq (IAS) in 2021 and agreed in 2025 to be taken private by Novacap for about $1.9 billion. B2B adtech, widely known among marketers, not consumers.

JDB Group is the Chinese company behind the Jiaduobao herbal tea brand, a red-can cooling herbal tea that became a leading beverage in China after a long trademark dispute over the Wong Lo Kat (Wanglaoji) name with Guangzhou Pharmaceutical. Based in Beijing, it sells beverages through distributors and retailers across China. Funding of about CNY 2 billion is shown for 2017. Very strong consumer brand recognition in China, though it lost market share after the dispute.

ngena is a network-as-a-service company that delivers software-defined WAN (SD-WAN) connections across multiple carriers to multinational enterprises, selling managed connectivity under one contract. Crunchbase shows a Boulder, Colorado location and funding of $286 million in January 2021. Customers are large corporations. B2B telecom brand with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Nuvia was a US semiconductor start-up, based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2019 by Apple chip veterans Gerard Williams III, John Bruno and Manu Gulati, designing high-performance Arm-based server processors. Qualcomm acquired it in March 2021 for about $1.4 billion, and its Oryon CPU cores power Snapdragon X laptop chips. It raised about $293 million before the acquisition. B2B chip technology with no consumer brand.

Ontic is a US protective intelligence and risk management software company, based in Austin, Texas, whose platform brings together threat, insider risk and security data for corporate security teams. It has grown partly through acquisitions, with about $287 million of funding by August 2025. Customers are large enterprises and public agencies. B2B security software with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Orica is an Australian company, based in Melbourne, that is the world's largest provider of commercial explosives and blasting systems for mining, quarrying and infrastructure, plus ground support and chemicals such as ammonium nitrate and sodium cyanide. It operates in over 100 countries, with revenue about AUD 7 billion. Listed on the ASX (ORI). B2B mining services brand, with little consumer awareness.

Pagoda (Baiguoyuan) is a Chinese fruit retail chain, based in Shenzhen, founded in 2001, which operates thousands of stores selling fresh fruit across the country, supplied by its own sourcing. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023 (2411), with Crunchbase showing CNY 1.9 billion raised by 2018. Customers are Chinese urban households. Strong consumer recognition in China, with limited reach outside.

Protecht is an Australian enterprise risk management software and training company, based in Sydney and founded in 1999, whose Protecht ERM platform helps banks, insurers and other regulated firms manage risks and compliance. Customers are across Australia, the UK and North America. Crunchbase shows about $310 million in funding, latest in March 2025. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

Quickline Communications is a UK fibre and fixed wireless broadband provider, based in Hull (Kingston upon Hull), serving homes and businesses in rural areas of Yorkshire and Lincolnshire and extending elsewhere, as an alternative network operator. It is private, with GBP 250 million of funding shown in August 2024, much of it likely infrastructure debt. Regional consumer broadband brand with limited national awareness.

Restor3d is a US medical device company, based in Durham, North Carolina, developing 3D-printed personalised orthopaedic implants and surgical instruments for foot and ankle, shoulder and spine, supported by AI and imaging. Customers are surgeons and hospitals. It raised about $292 million, latest in August 2025. Privately held. B2B medtech brand with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

ScaleFlux is a US storage technology company, based in Milpitas, California, known for computational storage drives and SSD controllers that process data within the drive, for data centres, cloud providers and AI workloads. Customers are cloud and enterprise operators. Funding shown is $287 million by February 2021. B2B hardware brand, with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

SecurityScorecard is a US cybersecurity ratings company, based in New York and founded in 2013, whose platform scores organisations' security posture and third-party risk using outside-in data, plus supply chain risk tools and threat intelligence. Customers are enterprises, insurers and governments. It raised about $292 million, with a 2021 round. Privately held. B2B brand, known in security and risk circles, not by consumers.

Shift Technology is a French artificial intelligence software company, based in Paris and founded in 2014, providing AI-native decision automation, fraud detection and claims handling software to insurers worldwide. Customers are over 100 insurers in 25 countries, paying subscriptions. It raised about $320 million, with a $220 million Series D in 2021. Privately held. B2B insurtech brand with no consumer awareness.

Shukun Technology is a Chinese artificial intelligence medical imaging company, based in Beijing, whose software helps analyse CT and other scans for cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and is used in hospitals across China. It raised about $296 million by August 2021. Customers are hospitals and health authorities, paying for software and services. B2B healthcare AI with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Snowball Finance (Xueqiu) is a Chinese investment social network and financial information platform, based in Beijing, where retail investors share stock views and buy funds and brokerage services through the app. It was founded in 2010 and raised about $293 million, with the last round in December 2020. Customers are Chinese retail investors. Strong awareness among Chinese retail investors, not widely known abroad.

Spectrum Brands is a US consumer products group, based in Middleton, Wisconsin, with brands such as Remington (shavers), George Foreman grills, Spectracide, Cutter and Hot Shot (home and garden), Tetra and Nature's Miracle (pet care), and Black+Decker-branded household appliances. The company sells through retailers like Walmart, Amazon and Home Depot worldwide, and has revenue of about $2.8 billion. Listed on the NYSE (SPB). Consumer brands widely known in the US.

ThredUp is a US online resale marketplace for secondhand clothing, shoes and accessories, based in Oakland, California, founded in 2009, where sellers send bags of clothing and buyers shop through a website and app, including resale-as-a-service for retailers such as Gap and Reformation. It listed on Nasdaq (TDUP) in 2021. Revenue is around $300 million. Customers are mainly women and families. Strong sustainable fashion brand in the US with large advertising.

Treasure Data is a US customer data platform company, based in Mountain View, California, founded in 2011 by Japanese engineers, whose cloud tools collect, unify and activate customer data for marketing. Arm bought it in 2018 for about $600 million, and in 2021 it was transferred to SoftBank Group as a separate company. Customers are large brands in retail, media and consumer goods. B2B software with no consumer awareness.

Unity Advisory is an advisory firm in London, England, which Crunchbase says offers corporate and tax advisory, and is shown with about $300 million in funding in April 2025. The input does not say who founded or owns it, which clients it serves or how many staff it has, and the funding figure suggests private equity or investor backing. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Up&Up is a US tech-enabled real estate platform, based in Brooklyn, New York, that lets homeowners and investors take part in property investment or capital release, with $284 million of funding by November 2021, likely including debt. Customers are homeowners and investors. The input does not make clear its model beyond that. Small fintech brand with limited consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Verastar was a UK services company, based in Sale, Cheshire, that sold business telecoms and related services to small businesses, with GBP 205 million of funding shown for December 2015. Customers were UK small and medium companies. The input does not give its ownership today, so its current status should be checked. B2B services brand, with little consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Weedmaps is a US cannabis technology platform, based in Irvine, California, where consumers find and order from dispensaries and delivery services, while businesses buy listings, advertising and WM Business software. It was founded in 2008 and listed on Nasdaq (MAPS) in 2021 through a SPAC. Revenue is around $190 million. Strong cannabis consumer brand in the US, restricted in mainstream advertising.

Yext is a US software company, based in New York and founded in 2006 by Howard Lerman, whose platform manages brand information such as locations and hours across search engines, maps and apps, and has moved into AI-powered search and answers for enterprises. It listed on the NYSE (YEXT) in 2017, with revenue of about $400 million. Customers are retailers, banks and healthcare brands. B2B marketing software, little consumer awareness.

Yugabyte is a US database software company, based in Sunnyvale, California, which develops the open-source YugabyteDB, a distributed SQL database for cloud-native applications, with a managed cloud service. Customers are enterprises including banks and retailers. It raised about $291 million, valued at $1.3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B developer brand, with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

ServiceMax is a US field service management software company, based in Pleasanton, California, whose cloud platform helps companies schedule technicians, manage assets and repair equipment. General Electric acquired it in 2016 for $915 million, and PTC bought it back from the private equity group Silver Lake in 2023 for about $1.46 billion. Customers are industrial and medical equipment manufacturers. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

1stdibs is a US online marketplace for luxury furniture, art, jewellery and fashion, based in New York, founded in 2000, connecting dealers and designers with high-end buyers. It earns commissions and fees, and listed on Nasdaq (DIBS) in 2021. Revenue is about $90 million. Customers are affluent collectors and interior designers. Recognised brand among luxury interior design and antiques buyers, but small in mass-market reach.

Alarabia OOH is a Saudi outdoor advertising company, based in Riyadh, operating billboards, digital screens and street furniture across Saudi cities, selling space to advertisers and agencies. Crunchbase shows SAR 972 million in funding in February 2025. Customers are brands and government advertisers. A well-known out-of-home media owner in Saudi Arabia, relevant for brand visibility, with limited public consumer-brand profile.

Alphaeon is a US company, based in Newport Beach, California, that built a consumer credit and digital platform for aesthetic and medical procedures, linked to the investor Strathspey Crown and a stake in Evolus (maker of the Jeuveau botulinum toxin). Customers are patients financing cosmetic and medical care, and practices. Crunchbase shows about $277 million raised by October 2020. Moderate recognition in the aesthetics industry, low among general consumers.

AppZen is a US AI software company, based in Santa Clara, California, whose platform automates expense reports, invoice and audit checks for finance teams, with large enterprises as customers. Founded in 2012, it raised about $280 million, including a Series D in 2021, and has a valuation above $1 billion. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Auvik Networks is a Canadian cloud-based network management software company, based in Waterloo, Ontario, whose platform automatically maps and monitors networks for managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams. Founded in 2011, it has thousands of MSP customers worldwide and raised about $283 million, latest in 2021. Privately held. B2B IT software with no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Banksteel.com is a Chinese iron and steel e-commerce platform, based in Baoshan, Shanghai, which started as a spin-off from Baosteel and serves steel traders and manufacturers with online trading, logistics, and supply chain finance. Funding of CNY 1.7 billion is shown for November 2017. Customers are steel buyers and sellers. B2B industrial platform, no consumer awareness. The figures here come from Crunchbase and may be out of date.

Bespin Global is a South Korean cloud and AI managed services provider, based in Seoul, helping enterprises migrate and operate systems on AWS, Google Cloud and Azure, and building AI services. Customers are Korean and Asian enterprises, public bodies and financial firms. Crunchbase shows about $253 million in funding, latest in December 2022. B2B IT services with no consumer awareness.

Carlsberg Marston's is a UK brewing company, based in Wolverhampton, formed in 2020 as a joint venture in which Carlsberg owns 60 percent and Marston's 40 percent, bringing together Carlsberg UK and Marston's beer business. It brews and distributes Carlsberg, Tuborg, Banks's, Hobgoblin, Wainwright and other brands, supplied to pubs and retailers. Customers are British pubs, supermarkets and consumers. Revenue is over GBP 600 million. Strong consumer beer brands in the UK.

China International Marine Containers (CIMC) is a Chinese manufacturer, based in Shenzhen, that is the world's largest maker of dry cargo containers and a major supplier of road transport vehicles, logistics and energy equipment, with offshore engineering. Customers are shipping lines, logistics groups and energy companies in over 100 countries. Revenue is around RMB 150 billion. Listed on the Shenzhen and Hong Kong stock exchanges (000039, 2039). B2B industrial brand, with no consumer awareness.

Copado is a US DevOps software company, based in Chicago, whose native Salesforce DevOps platform automates deployment, testing and release management for Salesforce teams, with an AI assistant. Customers are enterprise software and admin teams. It raised about $271 million, including a $140 million Series B in 2021, with investors such as Insight Partners. Privately held. B2B developer brand with no consumer awareness.

Covetrus is a US animal health technology and services company, based in Portland, Maine, formed in 2019 from the merger of Henry Schein Animal Health and Vets First Choice, supplying veterinarians with pharmaceuticals, consumables, practice management software and prescription management.
